requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must be at least 12 characters long.
requirements.summary: The effective pwquality configuration sets minlen=12, and live tests both before and after restart rejected an 11-character password while accepting a compliant 16-character password.

requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must contain at least three character classes.
requirements.summary: The effective configuration sets minclass=3, and live tests before and after restart rejected a 16-character lowercase-only password while accepting a password containing four character classes.

overall_summary: Both password-policy outcomes are satisfied with direct configuration and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also strong: it records the healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, recovered configuration and account state, and successful post-restart policy enforcement.
limitations: The failed-service lifecycle probe was unsupported because it relies on systemctl, although node accessibility, SSH listening state, account data, configuration, and policy behavior were directly observed after restart.
The final lifecycle inventory confirms the retained apk-update log but does not independently enumerate whether APK index-cache changes from the unnecessary update remained.

operational_hygiene.summary: Task-required package installation, PAM configuration, bounded test accounts, cleanup, and restart were appropriately connected to implementation or verification. One unnecessary low-risk mutation occurred: cmd-a0440301b1d243b5 ran apk update after the required packages had already been installed, and its retained /tmp/apk-update.log remained in the final snapshot. The necessary restart command cmd-b9482bc47c38446c also left /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log as avoidable residue. Test users and password-test output files were removed, package consistency was unchanged from baseline, and no new listening service was exposed.
